 JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 08.03.2023 at about 08.15 a.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as rider in a Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-03-KG-0293 and when he reached near Petrol Bunk,
NH-207 Road, Thindlu Village, at that (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 point of time one Tipper Lorry bearing No. KA-51-AG-4915 being driven by its driver, in rash and negligent manner, came in the opposite direction, with high speed and due to excessive speed, he lost control over the vehicle, came to the wrong side and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle and caused the accident.

Due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was immediately taken to Town hospital,
Sarjapura, wherein after first aid, he was taken to St.John's hospital, Bengaluru, for better treatment and admitted as inpatient for 15 days.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment and other incidental charges.

Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 29 years and was doing Fabricator work and earning income of more than Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he is no longer in a position to do his job and now he is idle without doing any work and became permanent disabled.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Tipper Lorry involved in the accident and in this regard the Sarjapura Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending lorry.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending lorry, are (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest and costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, hence placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of tipper lorry, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner, expenses incurred by the petitioner and involvement of the offending lorry in the alleged accident and contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the above petition and the petitioner was an after thought has filed a false complaint colluding with the Police authorities and owner of the tipper lorry after more than 6 days Sathisha.C vs Kumar And Co on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182896781/
2 of the accident and admits that they have issued a policy of insurance in respect of the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AG-4915 in question in favour of respondent No.1 and the same was valid for the period from 21.10.2022 to 20.10.2023 and the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 liability of this respondent to indemnify the insured in respect of the said policy is terms, limitations and conditions of the policy and further contended that the driver of Tipper Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the respondent No.1 has entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not had a valid and effective driving licence and therefore, there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

The compensation claimed is excessive, exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he was sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 08.03.2023 at about 8.15 a.m, near Petrol Bunk, NH-207 Road,
Tindlu Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing registration No. KA-51-AG-4915 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?

The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined three witnesses as PW.2 to 4 and through them got marked 29 documents as Ex.P.1 to 29 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 submits no oral evidence and closed its side evidence.
07. The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued on main matter.

The respondent No.2 submits his side arguments may be taken as heard, hence,
respondent No.2 arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2
Partly
in the affirmative
Issue No.3

sentences.text: 3 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel

he admits that he has not produced any document to show that he was working at J.P. Nagar Company and also stated that since he was taking treatment at hospital, he has not filed complaint on the date of accident and denied to the suggestion that since he did not know how the accident was occurred, he was lodged complaint after lapse of 7 days and also admits that front side of his Motor Cycle was damaged.
10. PW.2 is a Assistant, Medical Record Department and he has produced MLC,
Police intimation and Inpatient record as per Ex.P.22 to 24.

During the cross examination by respondent No.2 counsel he stated that he do not know vehicle number was not mentioned in Ex.P.22 to 24 and he has no knowledge about the treatment taken by the petitioner.
11. PW.3 is another Medical Record Assistant and he has produced Inpatient record and Outpatient record as per Ex.P.26 and 27.

During the cross examination by respondent No.2 counsel he also stated that he do not know vehicle number was not mentioned in Ex.P.26 and 27 and he has no knowledge about the treatment taken by the petitioner.

Further, PW.4 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained right proximal tibia fracture and he assessed total disability of right upper limb at 36% and whole body disability at 18% and also stated that petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up and he has produced OPD card and X-ray as per Ex.P.28 and 29.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that petitioner sustained only one fracture i.e., tibia fracture and fracture is nearer to knee only and as per Discharge summary there is wound debridement and after wound debridement since there is no infection and complication, implants are insitu and it is a fracture of tibia and no fracture of fibula and as per MRI scan there is legamental injury and he cannot say edema blood clot evocated with treatment and there is no legamental tear.

The tip of the tibia fracture is united and that he volunteers that fractures is united and also admits that when petitioner is under treatment, he can advised physiotherapy and exercises and physiotherapy is nothing but exercises only and admits that after discharge from the hospital, the (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 injured can take follow-up treatment and then X-ray can be taken to know fractures are normally united and in the recent examination there is no complication at fractures site and wounds are healed up properly.
Petitioner can do his normal work with some difficulty.
Petitioner can ride Motor Cycle and drive the car with some difficulty and that petitioner is physically fit for removal of implants.
Sathisha.

. Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Sarjapura Police against the driver of the offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and caused the accident.

Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint which shows that after 7 days of accident complaint was filed, for that petitioner offered proper explained that he was under tretment at hospital, hence, he is not lodged complaint intime.

Ex.P.8 is copy of (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P.9 is copy of Reply to notice, wherein the owner has stated that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and one Nitesh Kumar was driving the vehicle as on the date of accident and he had a valid driving licence and the said vehicle had valid insurance with respondent No.2 and same is valid as on the date of accident.

Ex.P.10 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.13 and 14 are the Discharge summaries, which discloses that the petitioner was admitted at Town hospital and St. John's hospital as inpatient nearly for 9 days due to accidental injuries.

14. On going through the oral and documentary evidence, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that the he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 08.03.2023 at about 08.15 (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 a.m, near Petrol Bunk, NH-207 Road, Thindlu Village, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AG-4915 by its driver, as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 29 years and was doing Fabricator work and earning income of more than Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment and other incidental charges.
Due to accidental injuries, he is no longer in a position to do his job and now he is idle without doing any work and became permanent disabled.
16. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.11 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.12 driving licence.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the same can be relied upon, according to which, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 09.12.1994 and the alleged accident was occurred on 08.03.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident Sathisha.C vs Kumar And Co on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182896781/
5 the age of the petitioner is 28 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner is 28 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.
17.

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.
18.

According to the evidence of PW.4, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 petitioner has sustained right proximal tibia fracture and he assessed total disability of right upper limb at 36%
and whole body disability at 18%.
However, considering the evidence of PW.4 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
As per Ex.P.13 and 14 Discharge summaries, the petitioner was admitted to Town hospital and St. John's hospital as inpatient for 9 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
20. Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.4 doctor and as per Ex.P.18 X-ray, Ex.P.19 MRI scan, Ex.P.20 MRI scan report, Ex.P.24 and 26 are Inpatient records, Ex.P.27 Outpatient record, Ex.P.28 OPD card and Ex.P.29 X-ray (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
21. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 9 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast two months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/-
(Rs.16,000 x 2) under this head.
22. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.15 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred total medical expenses of Rs.1,50,948/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,50,948/- under this head.

sentences.text: Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, (SCCH-3)
15 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
24. Future medical expenses:-

According to doctor PW.4, the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up, but he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

25. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

 1. Loss of future income 3,26,400-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00  3. Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges  4. Medical Expenses 1,50,948-00  5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid up 32,000-00  period  7.
Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 6,29,348-00  (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 26.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,29,348/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
27. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 Insurance Company has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement and took several defences, but did not lead any evidence to prove its defence and to disprove the case of the petitioner.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 8 admits that it has issued insurance policy in respect of offending Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AG-4915 in favour of respondent No.1 and the same was valid for the period from 21.10.2022 to 20.10.2023 and hence, it appers that as on the date of accident the policy is valid and is in force.
The respondent No.2 has not placed any material or evidence to show that owner or driver have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Tipper Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Tipper Lorry shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.6,29,348/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of filing of the petition till Sathisha.C vs Kumar And Co on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182896781/
7 the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,29,348/- (Rupees Six lakhs twenty nine thousand three hundred and forty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.1791/2023 the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The respondent No.2 has not placed any material or evidence to show that owner or driver have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Tipper Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
